def.name: Clear Practice Cutaway
def.note: Two pins, generous tolerances, nothing hidden. Start here.

def.name: Clear Practice Cutaway II
def.note: A third chamber, and a deeper cut to reach.

def.name: Brasswell No.1 Luggage
def.note: The lock on every suitcase ever made. It is not trying very hard.

def.name: Brasswell Bike Padlock
def.note: Four chambers and a wide bitting spread. Rakes beautifully.

def.name: Northgate Shed Padlock
def.note: Tighter than it looks. The first lock that will punish a heavy hand.

def.name: Brasswell 3-Wheel Luggage
def.note: Every suitcase you have ever owned. Pull the shackle and read the wheels with your thumb.

def.name: Northgate 5-Pin Cabinet
def.note: Five chambers. You will need a hook that reaches all of them.

def.name: Kestrel Door Cylinder
def.note: The lock on a million front doors, and no harder than one.

def.name: Ironhold Laminated Pad
def.note: One serrated pin, hiding among four honest ones. Which one is it?

def.name: Ironhold Spool Trainer
def.note: Two spools, nothing else. Made for learning what a false set feels like.

def.name: Kestrel Serrated Trainer
def.note: Every one of these pins will lie to you four times on the way up.

def.name: Northgate Commercial
def.note: Two spools and a serrated. The first lock that really needs a plan.

def.name: Halberd Deadbolt
def.note: Three spools. Back the tension off or it will fight you all day.

def.name: Ironhold Mushroom Pad
def.note: Mushrooms shove harder than spools. A light hand is the only hand.

def.name: Kestrel Pro Cylinder
def.note: Six chambers, five of them lying. The end of Tier 3, and it knows it.

def.name: Halberd Tight-Tolerance 5
def.note: Two spools, a mushroom and a serrated. Four false sets on one of them, and a wall.

def.name: Kestrel Slimline 5
def.note: Three slim spools. Every lie is a short one — keep moving.

def.name: Ironhold Combination Chain
def.note: Four wheels, and one digit on each that feels right and is not.

def.name: Meridian Euro Profile
def.note: The cylinder on half the front doors in Europe. Three spools and a mushroom.

def.name: Halberd Anti-Bump 6
def.note: Four serrated and two spools. Twenty false sets on the way up, give or take.

def.name: Halberd Sidebar Cylinder
def.note: Three chambers carry a sidebar gate. Set them wrong and the plug simply will not turn.

def.name: Halberd Sovereign
def.note: Seven chambers, every one of them a security pin, in a keyway that fits nothing.

def.name: Halberd T-Bar 6
def.note: One of everything the trade ever put in a chamber.

def.name: Meridian Strongbox Wheels
def.note: Twelve false gates across four wheels. Every third digit is a lie with good manners.
